title: Exponential time differencing for matrix-valued dynamical systems: global convergence of the METD$p$ scheme (Theorem 2)
author: Nayef Shkeir, Tobias Grafke
work: Exponential time differencing for matrix-valued dynamical systems
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 2 (source0.tex lines 457-473, source label thm:metdp_global), the global convergence theorem of the arbitrary-order matrix exponential time differencing scheme METD_p for matrix-valued evolution equations. The retained complete proof (lines 475-612) is a genuine 138-line numerical-analysis argument, not a routine verification: the update map is written in defect form, the one-step defect is estimated through the local defect theorem, the error is split into an interpolation and a commutator-truncation part with an explicit Lipschitz bound, a linear inhomogeneous error recursion is solved, the accumulated nonlinear terms are bounded by a discrete Gronwall-type estimate, and the startup error is propagated to a global C h^p bound on [0,T]. The residual difficulty is the assembly of these estimates under only the two standing assumptions plus [L,R]=0, with every constant tracked as independent of h and n; this is research-level numerical analysis rather than an ordinary PhD qualifying exercise, where such stability and consistency estimates are quoted rather than proved.
